# Northstar Supply: synthetic sales definitions



All data and report metadata are fictional. No real customer data is included.

The platform metadata is normalized fixture content, not native validated app exports.



- Ordered value: order-line quantity multiplied by unit price; order-date basis.

  Includes orders without invoices. This is a bookings measure, not recognized revenue.

- Invoiced sales: invoice-line ExtendedPrice minus TaxAmount; invoice-date basis.

  This simplified demo calls that revenue, without claiming accounting revenue recognition.

- ExtendedPrice includes tax in the synthetic invoice dataset.

- No currencies, discounts, returns or cancellations are modeled.

- Customers and products are shared between the two reporting paths.

- A product may belong to multiple stock groups. There is no designated primary group

  or approved allocation weighting. Group totals are therefore not necessarily additive.

- A proposed daily customer/product product must specify its date basis, tax treatment

  and grain. Do not silently substitute orders for invoices or invent missing dates.

- Qlik Sales Performance uses orders. Spotfire Customer Sales uses invoices.

  Both use all loaded dates and amounts excluding tax; differing tax treatment is not

  an explanation for a difference between these particular two synthetic reports.

JOIN HACKATHON_D2K_PREWORK.RAW.INVOICELINES l ON l.INVOICEID=i.INVOICEID

Need versions; fetch full docs.
The measure traces all the way back to two invoice-line columns: it is the sum of `INVOICELINES.EXTENDEDPRICE − INVOICELINES.TAXAMOUNT`, shown per customer name. Every step below comes from a document I read in full. All of these files are synthetic, normalized test fixtures, not real Spotfire or HANA exports.

**Lineage chain (source-backed)**

| # | Step | Evidence (doc_id / path / version) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Visual `SYN_VIZ_CUSTOMER` "Customer invoiced sales": value = `Sum([SalesAmount])`, category = `[CUSTOMERNAME]`, data table = `InvoiceSales`, all loaded dates, no filters, no currency | CONNECTED_a5086dc0ef985e23 / fixtures/spotfire/customer_sales.metadata.json / 46742043d0c70b3e9492aca16f0c3fc04404c1db0bc14e334978b2674f172357 |
| 2 | Calculated column `SalesAmount` = `[INVOICED_SALES_EX_TAX]`; the `InvoiceSales` table comes from `fixtures/spotfire/customer_sales.source.sql` | same document |
| 3 | That SQL selects `INVOICED_SALES_EX_TAX` and `CUSTOMERNAME` from `"SYNTHETIC_SALES"."CV_INVOICE_SALES"` | CONNECTED_1055b17d75582621 / fixtures/spotfire/customer_sales.source.sql / f67352b5a51bba4566da228ea9c31326007138b0e8e05aabca4de2686370f561 |
| 4 | In model `CV_INVOICE_SALES`: `INVOICED_SALES_EX_TAX = l.EXTENDEDPRICE − l.TAXAMOUNT` (l = INVOICELINES), and `CUSTOMERNAME = c.CUSTOMERNAME` (c = CUSTOMERS). The model's grain is INVOICELINEID | CONNECTED_c321fb5572f5ed86 / fixtures/hana/CV_INVOICE_SALES.model.xml / d33d0ec9211725e359b399623b46396df45aca42fac9800473bebb08cc061ce3 |
| 5 | Joins, all inner and many-to-one: `l.INVOICEID = i.INVOICEID` (INVOICES), `i.CUSTOMERID = c.CUSTOMERID`, `l.STOCKITEMID = p.STOCKITEMID` (STOCKITEMS) | same document |

**Source columns reached:** `INVOICELINES.EXTENDEDPRICE`, `INVOICELINES.TAXAMOUNT`, `CUSTOMERS.CUSTOMERNAME`. The join keys are `INVOICELINES.INVOICEID`, `INVOICES.INVOICEID`, `INVOICES.CUSTOMERID`, `CUSTOMERS.CUSTOMERID` and `STOCKITEMID`.

**Gaps (missing or unsupported evidence)**
- **Physical table location:** the model lists bare table names with no database or schema. A separate report view, Customer invoiced sales (doc CUSTOMER_INVOICE_SALES), uses `HACKATHON_D2K_PREWORK.RAW.CUSTOMERS / INVOICES / INVOICELINES` with the same formula. That view is not part of the Spotfire chain, so the RAW schema is supporting evidence only. I also didn't fetch that view's full document, so I can't give its version.
- **Grouping by customer:** the visual groups by `CUSTOMERNAME`, which is a label, while customer identity is `CUSTOMERID`. If two customers share a name, their totals would be combined; nothing in the evidence rules that out.
- **Tax treatment:** that ExtendedPrice includes tax, so subtracting TaxAmount excludes it, is stated in definitions.md. I saw that document only in search results and didn't fetch it in full, so I can't give its version.
- **Not shown in the chain:** none of these documents show a native platform deployment or a complete enterprise lineage.

I didn't propose or build a candidate data product, so there are no candidate or validation IDs to report.
